description:
Reconcile the run-activity identifier with KINP §3.1's grammar — IMP-7, and a defect koine's own examples demonstrate.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TEXT (2026-09-12, before this tasklist was authored). Every leg holds, and the two spellings do not even agree with each other.

WHAT §3.1 FIXES. `<kind>` is 'one of: `ent` | `claim` | `asset` | `world` | `agent` | `src`' — a closed list of six. `<local-id>` is 'opaque within the namespace; `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*` (lowercase, percent-encode anything else)' — a charset that admits letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen, and NOT the solidus.

WHAT THE EXAMPLES ACTUALLY WRITE.
- KFT §5.2's worked PROV activity is `orchestrator:activity:ft-run/9f2a` (and §3's job field, and §6's `of_job`, use the same form). Kind `activity` is not in the enum; the `/` is not in the charset. TWO violations.
- KINP's own §7.1 assertion-envelope example writes the same thing as `analyzer:run/1a2b`, and §3.4's namespace-registry table gives the `analyzer` row as 'Run-scoped locals: `analyzer:run/<runid>`'. No kind segment at all, and the `/` again.
- KMI §2's envelope example carries `"produced_by": "analyzer:run/1a2b"`, so the second spelling is load-bearing on a third spec.

SO THE TWO DO NOT AGREE WITH EACH OTHER, and a consumer cannot pattern-match a run activity across participants. This is already IMP-7 in `docs/reference/implementability-audit.md` §3.3 — filed as a gap against KINP §3.1 vs KINP §7.1, KMI §2, KFT §3/§5/§6 and the schema — which also notes that `src` IS in the enum and is used as a kind NOWHERE. A producer that had to mint one has since reproduced it from the outside and found no spelling satisfying §3.1 and §5.2 at once.

WHY IT IS A `fix` AND NOT A FEATURE. Nothing new is being contracted. A normative grammar and three worked examples in three specs disagree, and every `prov` record depends on the id: KINP §7.1's envelope carries `prov.activity`, KFT §5.2 makes the run a PROV activity and the reproducibility anchor (FT-C), and §6's `of_job` is 'what makes the leg attributable'.

EITHER FIX IS ACCEPTABLE; DOING NEITHER IS NOT. Admit `activity` to the §3.1 enum and widen the local charset to admit the separator the examples use; OR state the run-activity spelling normatively in §3.1 and correct the §3.4 row to match. Either way the two examples MUST be reconciled to one spelling, and the schema checked against it.

userStories.title: Decide the run-activity spelling, and make §3.1 normative about it
userStories.description: Two routes, one outcome: a run activity has exactly one spelling that §3.1 admits.
acceptanceCriteria: KINP §3.1 admits the run-activity identifier — either by adding `activity` to the `<kind>` enum and widening `<local-id>`'s charset to admit the separator the examples use, or by stating the run-activity spelling normatively in §3.1 — and the choice is recorded with its reasoning.

Whichever route is taken, the resulting grammar ADMITS a run activity and the text says so explicitly, so an implementer minting one meets a rule instead of a contradiction. The immutability consequence is weighed on the record: identifiers already minted under either spelling must keep resolving, as §3.4 requires of a published prefix.

The audit's companion observation is answered rather than left standing: `src` is in the §3.1 enum and is used as a kind nowhere in this repo. Either it gets a stated use or the record says why an unused kind stays.

GATES: `node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs`, `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `node scripts/check-schemas.mjs`, `node scripts/check-registry.mjs`, `node scripts/check-tasklist-categories.mjs` and `bash scripts/check-roadmap-truth.sh` all green, with the observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: KINP 0.5.0: §3.1 enum gains `activity`; run-activity spelling stated normatively as `<namespace>:activity:<local-id>`; `<local-id>` charset deliberately NOT widened (IRI path-segment invertibility), with the rejected route recorded. Immutability weighed: no prefix moves, no claim id moves, nothing conformant invalidated. `src` answered (stays; name collision with the `src(...)` annotation; re-open condition stated). §4-§11 byte-unchanged, proven by section-slice shasum diff. GATES all green: doc-integrity OK (60 md files, 1647 links, all 3 status tables match headers, identity 0.5.0 candidate); doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main; schemas OK (9 schemas, 278 positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures); registry OK (29 relations); tasklist-categories OK (11 tasklists); roadmap coverage/stale/park OK (51 completed, 41 merged). `chief verify` exit 0 RECORDED.

userStories.title: One spelling, everywhere it appears
userStories.description: The two forms are load-bearing in three specs and a schema. Reconciling the grammar without reconciling the examples fixes nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: Every occurrence of a run-activity id in this repo uses the ONE decided spelling: KINP §7.1's assertion-envelope example and §3.4's `analyzer` namespace row, KFT §3's `job`, §5.2's worked PROV activity and §6's `of_job`, and KMI §2's `produced_by`. A grep proving no occurrence was missed is recorded, not asserted.

The schemas are checked against the decided spelling and updated where they constrain or exemplify it — `schemas/provenance.schema.json` and `schemas/finetune-job.schema.json` at minimum — and `node scripts/check-schemas.mjs` is green over the result with its observed counts recorded (today: 9 schemas, 278 schema positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures).
Any schema fixture carrying a run-activity id is updated with it, so the fixtures keep carrying production shapes rather than a form the spec no longer admits.

Version moves for every spec touched are decided under each spec's own rules and recorded with reasoning; where a version moves, all three status mirrors (`README.md`, `specs/README.md`, `ECOSYSTEM.md`) move with it, which `check-doc-integrity.mjs` enforces.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: One spelling everywhere: `<namespace>:activity:<local-id>`. KINP examples corrected (§3.4 `analyzer` row, §4.2 `same_as` src(), §7.1 envelope, §7.2 `produced_by`) inside 0.5.0; KMI 0.3.5->0.3.6 (patch: §2 envelope, §6 bridge src()); KFT 0.7.0->0.7.1 (patch: §3 `job`, §3.4 `resume.of_job`, §5.2 PROV activity, §6 telemetry). Schemas: finetune-job.schema.json `kinpId` description example moved; its PATTERN deliberately NOT tightened (a KINP id may be world-scoped, so the third group must stay permissive) with the reason on the record; provenance.schema.json checked and carries no activity id, so unchanged. Fixtures updated: finetune-job.json x3 (incl. dataset.knowledge[].provenance.run, which the obvious grep misses) and participant-self-description.json. Scenarios reconciled too: e2e-worlds-to-fabric.md x4, kft-resume-checkpoint.md x4. GREP PROOF recorded in progress.txt: 0 legacy spellings remain outside records-of-the-defect (ROADMAP task row, CLAUDE.md narrative, KINP 3.1 'not admitted' paragraph + changelogs, implementability-audit, interop-trial). Version moves: both patch (value-only, no clause moves, no asset/claim id moves, 0.4.0 stays spent on the EDL removal, KFT gates restated and neither moves); all three status mirrors moved and check-doc-integrity enforces them. GATES all green: doc-integrity OK (60 md files, 1653 links, all 3 status tables match headers, fine-tuning 0.7.1 / media-interchange 0.3.6 candidate); doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main; schemas OK (9 schemas, 278 positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures); registry OK (29 relations); tasklist-categories OK (11 tasklists); roadmap coverage/stale/park OK (51 completed, 41 merged). `chief verify` exit 0 RECORDED for tree ed870906.

userStories.title: Close IMP-7, and record the outside reproduction
userStories.description: The finding is koine's own, and it has now been independently hit. Close it where it lives.
acceptanceCriteria: IMP-7 is marked closed in `docs/reference/implementability-audit.md` §3.3 with what landed and where, and the outside reproduction is recorded as corroboration — a producer that had to mint a run activity and found no spelling satisfying §3.1 and §5.2 at once.
The producer is referred to BY ROLE, never by repository or product name — this repo is public and its rows are role-scoped and product-agnostic by design.
The audit's own summary line — that a third party cannot parse or mint identifiers unambiguously (IMP-6, IMP-7) — is updated to reflect what this closes and what IMP-6 still leaves open.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: IMP-7 closed in docs/reference/implementability-audit.md §3.3 as a dated `#### IMP-7 is CLOSED (2026-09-12)` subsection, with the finding's own 2026-08-18 text preserved verbatim (the discipline doc-drift-corrections.md § records: this document corrects its counts, never its findings). Records what landed and where — KINP 0.5.0 §3.1 (`activity` in the enum, the spelling stated normatively, the charset deliberately not widened with IMP-6's invertibility reason), the reconciled examples in KINP/KMI 0.3.6/KFT 0.7.1, the schema description + two fixtures, both patch bumps with no clause/asset/claim id moving — plus the migration rule, and the `src` companion observation answered. The outside reproduction is recorded as corroboration BY ROLE only (a **producer role** that had to mint a run activity and found no spelling satisfying KINP §3.1 and KFT §5.2 at once, reporting it as a proposed koine change per ADR-0008) — no repository or product name; the INT-3 closure paragraph is the precedent followed. A *What this closure does not do* block states the three things it does NOT close: IMP-8's third bullet (`cs:language:Q1860`), IMP-6 (which the fold cites rather than closes), and the twin's still-unenforced grammar. §4.2's summary bullet is split into the half that closed (minting) and the half that did not (parsing, IMP-6, the claim-identity-bearing one), verdict still *partially*; §3's preamble gains the dated-CLOSED grade convention; §6 records fifteen open, not sixteen; changelog entry added and the header's Updated date moved to 2026-09-12. interop-trial.md's audit row annotated 'closed 2026-09-12' with the observation column untouched. GATES all six green: doc-integrity OK (60 md files, 1659 relative links — exactly +6 for the 6 new links, all 3 status tables match headers); doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main; schemas OK (9 schemas, 278 positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures); registry OK (29 relations); tasklist-categories OK (11 tasklists); roadmap coverage/stale/park OK (51 completed, 41 merged). `chief verify` exit 0 RECORDED for tree 29b7a825.
